description: Believes || is logical OR (as in MySQL) rather than string concatenation in Postgres.
Believes 'a' || NULL yields 'a'; in fact concatenating with NULL yields NULL.
Confuses ILIKE with LIKE: thinks ILIKE uses regex, spans lines, or is index-friendly with a plain B-tree, rather than just being case-insensitive.
Mixes up psql meta-commands for listing objects (\dt, \dn, \l, \du, \dv, \df, \dx), e.g. thinking \dn lists tables.
Believes \c mydb creates the database or sets it as a persistent default, rather than reconnecting the session.
Believes \q commits an open transaction before exiting, rather than the transaction being rolled back.
Misreads psql toggles: thinks \x widens output or shows EXPLAIN/timing, or that \timing is something other than a per-query duration toggle.
Believes SERIAL creates a trigger, hidden counter column or identity constraint rather than a sequence with a default nextval().
Believes BIGSERIAL and SERIAL share the same integer range, when BIGSERIAL is 64-bit.
Believes inserting an explicit value into a GENERATED ALWAYS identity column succeeds or is silently overridden, rather than erroring without OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE.
Believes unquoted identifiers keep their case, rather than being folded to lowercase, and that double quotes behave like string quotes.
Believes VARCHAR(n) is measurably faster than TEXT in Postgres, when they perform essentially the same.
Believes CHAR(n) stores the value as-is or errors on shorter values, rather than padding with trailing spaces.
Believes tables created without a schema land in pg_catalog, information_schema or a 'default' schema rather than public (first on search_path).
Believes search_path controls file lookup, read permissions or databases, rather than the ordered schemas for resolving unqualified names.

Believes RETURNING on DELETE/UPDATE gives the old row for UPDATE, or misjudges what it returns (UPDATE returns new values, DELETE the deleted row); also thinks RETURNING * returns only keys or counts.
Believes ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING raises an error, upserts, or rolls back other rows, rather than silently skipping the conflicting row.
Believes the column list in ON CONFLICT (id) names columns to overwrite or index, rather than identifying the unique constraint/index to arbitrate on.
Believes Postgres arrays are 0-indexed, when they are 1-indexed by default, and misjudges slices and array_length.
Believes arrays are built with '[1,2,3]', ARRAY(1,2,3) or LIST(), rather than ARRAY[...] or the '{...}' text form.
Confuses jsonb -> (returns jsonb) with ->> (returns text), or believes they differ in nesting depth or error behavior.
Believes @> tests byte equality, key presence only, or ordering, rather than structural containment of the right value in the left.
Believes NOW() advances between calls in one transaction, when it returns the transaction start time; only clock_timestamp() changes.
Confuses return types of CURRENT_DATE (date) and NOW() (timestamptz), or related date/time functions like to_char, to_date, date_trunc and EXTRACT.
Misunderstands COALESCE (first non-NULL argument) and NULLIF (returns NULL when arguments are equal), e.g. expecting errors or zero.
Believes DISTINCT ON picks a deterministic row without a matching ORDER BY, or that it behaves like plain DISTINCT or returns only the key column.
Believes boolean columns accept bare integers or arbitrary strings like 'yes'/'maybe' without casting, or that TRUE/FALSE are case-sensitive.
Believes CHECK constraints only apply on insert, only warn, or hide failing rows, rather than being enforced on every insert and update.
Believes plain EXPLAIN runs the query and reports real runtime, when only EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes it.
Confuses pg_catalog (Postgres-specific, richer) with information_schema (SQL-standard, portable) views and their advantages.
Misreads session info functions: current_user as OS user or original login role, version() as an integer or client version, current_database() as an OID or default.
Believes :: is schema qualification, an alias or an assertion, or that CAST and :: always behave identically, rather than :: being cast shorthand.
Misunderstands INTERVAL as integer seconds or text, or thinks NOW() + INTERVAL is an error, drops time, or AGE returns an integer.
Believes generate_series or unnest return one row holding an array or a count, rather than a set of rows.
Misunderstands aggregates like string_agg and array_agg, e.g. thinking string_agg sorts, splits, or array_agg deduplicates.
Believes <> handles NULL like any value, or that IS DISTINCT FROM treats NULL as empty string or errors, rather than being NULL-safe comparison.
Believes nextval() values are returned on rollback or that nextval only previews, when sequence advances are non-transactional and leave gaps.
Confuses CREATE TYPE ENUM, composite types and CREATE DOMAIN with CHECK constraints, lookup tables, arrays or documentation-only aliases.
Believes wrapping an indexed column in a function or cast (lower(email), id::text, left(sku,8)) still uses its plain B-tree index, and that count(*)>0 is as cheap as EXISTS.
